problems.title: The sign is not determined by a fourth-angle cosine
problems.question: Find tan x+cot x if cos4x=7/9.
problems.idea: Determine the square of sin2x and retain both signs.
steps: sin²2x=1/9, so sin2x=±1/3.
The required value is therefore ±6. Both signs occur for real x satisfying the given condition.
problems.note: No quadrant restriction is supplied, so a single sign cannot be selected.

problems.title: A parameter equation at its amplitude limit
problems.question: Find all a and x satisfying $\sqrt{2a^2+1}\cos x+\sqrt{4-a^2-2a}\sin x=-a^2+2a-3$.
problems.idea: The absolute value of a sine–cosine combination cannot exceed its amplitude.
formulas: A cos x+B sin x has range [−√(A²+B²),√(A²+B²)].
steps: Set t=(a−1)²≥0. The squared amplitude is a²−2a+5=t+4, while the right side is −(t+2).
Solvability requires (t+2)²≤t+4, equivalently t(t+3)≤0. Hence t=0 and a=1, which satisfies the square-root domains.
The equation becomes √3 cos x+sin x=−2, or 2cos(x−π/6)=−2.
Thus x−π/6=π+2kπ.

problems.title: Factor a trigonometric inequality
problems.question: Solve $4\sin^2 2x\sin4x+4\sin5x\ge2\sin4x+\sin2x$.
problems.idea: Combine the first two sin4x terms, then use sum-to-product.
steps: Move the right side left. The expression becomes −sin8x+4sin5x−sin2x.
This factors as 2sin5x(2−cos3x).
The second factor is always positive, so the inequality is equivalent to sin5x≥0.

problems.title: Which equal-edge pyramid has the greatest surface area?
problems.question: Every edge of a convex pyramid equals a. Find the height of the one with greatest total surface area.
problems.idea: Its base vertices lie on a circle and all consecutive chords are equal, so the base is regular.
formulas: Base circumradius R=a/[2sin(π/n)]; height²=a²−R²; total area=a²[n cot(π/n)/4+n√3/4].
steps: A nonzero height requires R<a, so sin(π/n)>1/2. For integer n≥3 this permits n=3,4,5.
The total-area coefficients are √3 for n=3, 1+√3 for n=4, and (5/4)(cot36°+√3) for n=5. The pentagonal case is largest.
Subtract R² from a² to obtain h²=a²(5−√5)/10.
problems.answer: h=a√[(5−√5)/10], for the regular pentagonal pyramid.

problems.title: A square pyramid from its dihedral angle
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has height 1 and interior dihedral angle 120° between adjacent lateral faces. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Use normals to two adjacent faces.
formulas: If the base half-edge is t, suitable outward normals are (1,0,t) and (0,1,t); cos60°=t²/(1+t²).
steps: The outward-normal angle is 180°−120°=60°. Thus t²/(1+t²)=1/2, so t=1.
The base edge is 2, and each face altitude is √(1²+1²)=√2.
Four triangular faces have area 4·(2√2/2).

problems.title: Principal values of arccos
problems.question: Find tanα if $5\alpha-7\arccos(\cos\alpha)=0$.
problems.idea: The principal arccos value lies in [0,π].
formulas: The equation implies 0≤α≤7π/5; arccos(cosα)=α on [0,π], and 2π−α on [π,2π].
steps: In the first interval, 5α=7α gives α=0.
In the second, 5α=7(2π−α), giving α=7π/6, which is allowed.
The tangents at these two angles are 0 and 1/√3.
problems.note: Both values satisfy the equation; no condition excludes α=0.

problems.title: Factor a mixed sine and cosine equation
problems.question: Solve $\cos2x+\cos5x-\cos8x=\sin10x+\sin3x$.
steps: The first factor gives sin5x=1/2, hence x=π/30+2kπ/5 or x=π/6+2kπ/5.
For the second, sin3x=sin(π/2−5x).
The two sine-equality branches give x=π/16+kπ/4 or x=−π/4+kπ.

problems.title: Parallel sections split lateral area by squared scale
problems.question: Two planes parallel to a pyramid’s base divide its altitude, starting at the apex, in ratio 9:6:10. In what ratio do they divide the lateral area?
problems.idea: Similar pyramids have surface areas proportional to squared lengths.
formulas: Distances from apex are 9,15,25 in common units; cumulative areas are proportional to 9²,15²,25².
steps: The top piece has proportional area 81.
The middle band has 225−81=144.
The bottom band has 625−225=400.

problems.title: Two isosceles right diagonal sections
problems.question: A pyramid has rhombus base ABCD, and ASC and BSD are isosceles right triangles. Find the cosine of the rhombus’s acute angle.
problems.idea: The locations of the right angles matter. Classify the possible isosceles-right sections.
steps: If the right angle of ASC is at S, then u=0 and v²+h²=p². If instead it is at A or C, then u=±p and v²+h²=4p².
Likewise BSD gives either v=0,u²+h²=q², or v=±q,u²+h²=4q².
If both sections use the same type, these equations force p=q and a square base. A rhombus with an acute angle must therefore use different types.
For example u=0,v=q gives h²=4q² and p²=5q². The other mixed type swaps p,q.
The acute rhombus angle has cosine |p²−q²|/(p²+q²)=4/6.
problems.note: If both right angles are intended to be at S, the base is a square and has no acute interior angle. The value 2/3 uses the mixed placement allowed by the printed wording.

problems.title: A trig system on the first quadrant
problems.question: Solve $\cos(x-y)=\cos x\sin y+\cos x$, $\sin(x+y)=\sin x\cos y+\sin y$, with $x,y\in[0,\pi/2]$.
formulas: sin(x+y)=sin x cos y+cos x sin y.
steps: The second equation reduces to sin y(cos x−1)=0, so y=0 or x=0.
When y=0, the first equation is cos x=cos x, valid for every allowed x.
When x=0, the first equation is cos y=sin y+1. In the first quadrant this forces y=0.
